title: Put the studio's entrance and loop durations on the motion tokens
body:
## Summary
`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/adopt.css` times its motion with five literal durations (260ms, 320ms, 1.2s, 1s, 1.4s) where the overlay requires duration tokens.

## Description
The overlay (.claude/scan-sweep/config.md) says spacing, colour, radius, duration and easing come from `src/styles/app.css` tokens. adopt.css uses `animation: ad-arrive 260ms` on every feed item (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/adopt.css:143`), `ad-arrive 320ms` on the showcase (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/adopt.css:843`), and the loops `ad-beat 1.2s` (`:284`), `ad-beat 1s` (`:464`), `ad-sweep 1.4s` (`:784`). The tokens on offer are `--duration-fast` (150ms), `--dur-depth` (360ms) and `--dur-settle` (600ms); no loop token exists. Fixed looks like: the two entrances on `--dur-depth` (or a new entrance token), the three loops on one new loop token, and a stylesheet test (as `chores.css.test.ts` does for chores.css) that fails on a literal duration in adopt.css. Calm and reduced motion are already honoured (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/adopt.css:8`, `apps/desktop/src/styles/app.css:878`).

## Flow
- read adopt.css for every animation/transition duration
- pick the token per site (entrance vs loop) - the choice changes how fast the feed arrives, so it is a design call
- write adopt.css.test.ts: no literal ms/s duration outside var(); seed one and watch it fail
- replace the five literals

## Expected impact
A person sees the studio's arrivals move at the pace of the rest of the depth frame; the token test keeps the next literal out. Could break: a slower entrance (360ms vs 260ms) reads sluggish on a long feed.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - adopt.css obeys the duration-token rule
Before: 5 literal durations in adopt.css (grep)
After: 0 by the same grep, once the token choice is made
Method: probe - counted by grep; the After needs the token choice (entrance speed is taste), so it was not built in the round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: adopt.css.test.ts: count literal durations outside var() in adopt.css; 5 before, 0 after; a seeded literal goes red

title: Mark a refused composer line as not sent and let it be sent again
body:
## Summary
A composer line the daemon refused stays in the conversation drawn exactly like a sent one, with only an error line under it; the person cannot tell it never reached her, and must retype it.

## Description
`actions.say` dispatches `said` before the POST (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/session.ts`, say) and on a refusal dispatches `unsaid` (the stale mark only, commit 6eee205d) and an error line; the `you` bubble (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/conversation.tsx`, Item case "you") has no status. The front door's `say` (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/intake/session.ts`) is the same, and `hasSaid`/`needOf` (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/intake/state.ts:82`) count an unsent line as said. The doc bubble already has `sending|sent|failed` (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/state.ts`, FeedItem doc). Fixed looks like: `you` items carry `status: sent|failed`, a failed one says "not sent" and offers Send again (or returns the words to the box), and `hasSaid`/`needOf` and park's answer count skip failed lines.

## Flow
- type a line, press Send while the daemon refuses (offline)
- observe: the bubble reads as said, an error line follows, the words are gone from the box
- build: FeedItem you.status, the reducer marks it failed on unsaid, Item draws 'not sent' and a resend, intake hasSaid ignores failed lines
- tests: studio and intake, a refused line is marked and re-sendable

## Expected impact
The person sees which words she never got and re-sends them with one press; "Just decide for me" no longer opens on a line the daemon never heard. Could break: parked snapshots (park.ts counts `you` lines) must skip failed lines too.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a refused line is visibly unsent and recoverable
Before: 0 of 2 surfaces (studio, front door) mark a refused line; the words are lost from the box (reproduced in the studio.test.tsx case 8 setup)
After: 2 of 2, by behaviour tests (not written)
Method: simulation - walked on the case-8 flow; M across state, conversation, intake state and park, past this round's M-risk-3 line
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: studio.test.tsx + intake.test.tsx: a refused composer line is drawn 'not sent', Send again posts it, Just decide stays shut on a refused-only line (0/3 -> 3/3)

title: Leave a trace when closing an adopt or intake session fails
body:
## Summary
Every DELETE of an adopt or intake session is fire-and-forget with `.catch(() => {})` at eight sites; a failed close holds one of the daemon's three places and the next start fails `busy:` with nothing recorded about why.

## Description
The daemon keeps at most three live sessions of either kind (`src/athena/adopt/routes.py:11`, 429 `budget_exhausted` `busy:` at `src/athena/adopt/routes.py:218`). The desktop closes sessions on unmount, displacement, parked expiry, start-over and after the verdict, each swallowing the failure: `apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/session.ts` (the aborted start, the foreign or expired park, the unmount close, the displaced park, startOver) and `apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/intake/session.ts` (after the verdict, the aborted start, the unmount close). The comments say fire and forget by design (ADR 0179), but a failure that later changes an outcome ("Three conversations are already open with her") leaves no signal. Fixed looks like: one `closeQuietly(client, sid, why)` helper that records a failed close where the desktop records client faults, used at every site, and a test that a rejected close is recorded.

## Flow
- leave a studio while the daemon refuses the DELETE (a network blip)
- open three more conversations: the fourth start is `busy:`
- nothing anywhere says a close failed
- build: one helper, eight call sites, one test

## Expected impact
An operator reading the console after a 'busy' report sees which session failed to close and when. Could break: noise in tests whose fake close rejects.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed close leaves a trace
Before: 0 of 8 close sites record a failure (grep `catch(() => {})` in the two session hooks)
After: 8 of 8 through one helper (not built)
Method: probe - sites counted by grep; where the trace should go (console vs a diagnostics store) is a repo convention this round did not own
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
grep -n 'catch(() => {})' apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/session.ts apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/intake/session.ts -> 8 hits
src/athena/adopt/routes.py:218 return error(429, "budget_exhausted", f"busy: {exc}")
instrument: a session test with a close that rejects: the failure is recorded once per site (0/8 -> 8/8); needs the repo's chosen client-diagnostics sink

title: Say 'known' only for confirmed slots and name lane states in words
body:
## Summary
The case panel's headline counts guessed slots as "known" while its own legend and pills call them "my guess", and each research lane shows its raw wire status ("queued", "running", "skipped").

## Description
`SlotsBoard` prints `t.confirmed + t.guessed` "of N known" (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/casepanel.tsx:70`) beside a legend that separates confirmed from "my guess" (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/casepanel.tsx:95`), so the biggest number on the panel claims as known what the same panel calls a guess. `ResearchTray` prints `{l.status}` (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/adopt/casepanel.tsx:193`), the contract's enum word, while every other status in the studio is a word for people (STATUS_WORD, SOURCE_WORD in the same file). Fixed looks like: the count says what it counts ("N of M confirmed, K guessed" or "filled"), and a LANE_WORD record beside LANE_TONE.

## Flow
- open a studio with one confirmed and one guessed slot
- read '2 of 2 known' over a legend saying one is a guess
- watch a lane read 'queued' then 'running'

## Expected impact
The person trusts the headline because it agrees with the tiles under it. Could break: studio tests that read the count and the lane status text.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the panel's words agree with each other
Before: 2 strings on one panel that contradict it or expose code (the headline count, the lane status)
After: 0, once the wording is chosen
Method: probe - read on the panel; the replacement words are a product wording call, so not built
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: Let a chore adopted from a project carry its space_id to POST /adopt
body:
## Summary
`POST /adopt` accepts `space_id` (ADR 0225) and writes it into the case on approve, but `AdoptClient.start` never sends it, so a chore adopted while a project is active is saved to Athena's core.

## Description
The route reads `space_id` (`src/athena/adopt/routes.py:16`, "the project the chore is adopted in: the approve writes it into the case"; validated at `src/athena/adopt/routes.py:209`). `AdoptApi.start(playbookId, intro?, caseId?)` (`apps/desktop/src/lib/adopt-client.ts`, start) builds `{playbook_id, intro?, case_id?}` and no `space_id`; `ADOPT_ROUTES.start`'s comment (`apps/desktop/src/lib/adopt.ts:151`) omits it too. Linking happens only afterwards through `POST /adopt/cases/<proj>/space` (`apps/desktop/src/lib/spaces.ts:88`). Whether the studio should read the active project at start is a product decision: it is a capability the desktop does not have today.

## Flow
- make a project active, open a chore's studio, approve
- the case lands in core; the person links it by hand
- build: pass the active space to start, add `space_id` to the client and the route comment, a client test

## Expected impact
A chore made inside a project belongs to it without a second step. Could break: a case reopened while another project is active would move unless "" keeps its own (the route already does).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the adopt start carries the project the route accepts
Before: 1 field the route reads that the client never sends
After: 0
Method: probe - read both sides; building it adds a capability (the studio reading the active project), so it waits for a decision
Result: better
Gate: direction
